beats.text: THE DEPENDENT MACHINE
beats.label: THE QUESTION

beats.text: The answer sits inside a chain of specialized decisions and infrastructure.
beats.label: THE SYSTEM

beats.text: TSMC was founded on February 21, 1987, as the world's first dedicated semiconductor foundry.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Founder Morris Chang created TSMC to commercialise semiconductor research developed at Taiwan's Industrial Technology Research Institute.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Philips invested 58 million US dollars and licenced its production technology in exchange for a 27.6 percent stake in the new company.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: The Taiwanese government provided nearly half of TSMC's startup capital through its National Development Fund.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Texas Instruments and Intel both declined to build Taiwan's chip industry before the foundry was created.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: The foundry model separates chip design from fabrication, letting fabless design companies share advanced manufacturing capacity.
beats.label: PRIMARY

beats.text: TSMC's headquarters have sat in Hsinchu Science Park, Taiwan, since the company's founding.
beats.label: PRIMARY

beats.text: From 1994, TSMC grew revenue at a compound annual rate of about 17 percent for three decades.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC was the first foundry to bring 7-nanometre and then 5-nanometre chip production to market in volume.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC's N7+ process was the first commercially available extreme-ultraviolet lithography in the semiconductor industry.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In late 2022 TSMC began volume production of 3-nanometre logic at Tainan, offering up to 70 percent higher logic density than 5 nanometre.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: By late 2025 TSMC had moved to 2-nanometre production using gate-all-around nanosheet transistors, a shift away from FinFET designs.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: The 2-nanometre node offers a 10 to 15 percent performance boost or a 25 to 30 percent power reduction over enhanced 3 nanometre.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: The 5-nanometre node doubled transistor density and added 15 percent performance over the preceding generation.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC today produces chips on node sizes from 2 micrometres down to 3 nanometres across its wafer fabrication network.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC was the first producer to run ASML's extreme-ultraviolet lithography machines at high volume.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In 2014 TSMC led the foundry industry in high-performance 28-nanometre production, drawing orders from Qualcomm, MediaTek and Apple.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC holds a commanding majority of the global semiconductor foundry market, roughly 70 percent.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In 2025 TSMC generated revenue of 122 billion US dollars, with net income of 55 billion.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In 2023 TSMC earned net profit of about 838 billion Taiwan dollars on revenue above 2 trillion Taiwan dollars.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC serves as the main supplier for Apple, NVIDIA, Broadcom and Qualcomm.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Most fabless chip companies, including AMD, ARM and MediaTek, have relied on TSMC's foundry services.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Even integrated device makers such as Intel, NXP and Texas Instruments outsource some of their production to TSMC.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC is one of the world's largest non-US companies by market capitalisation.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC stock makes up about 30 percent of the Taiwan Stock Exchange's main index.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC's role as an AI supply-chain bottleneck means a single disruption could trigger another worldwide chip shortage.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: The company's growth since 2023 has been driven by the artificial intelligence boom and its role in the advanced chips AI needs.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In 2024 the United States was TSMC's largest market, nearly 69 percent of sales.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC raised its 2026 capital expenditure forecast to between 60 and 64 billion US dollars on strong AI chip demand.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Second-quarter 2026 profit rose 77 percent year on year, a record driven by demand for artificial-intelligence chips.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In 2020 TSMC announced a 12 billion US dollar fab in Phoenix, Arizona, at the time the most advanced fab in the United States.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In December 2022 TSMC said it would triple its Arizona investment to about 40 billion US dollars across three plants.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In April 2024 the Biden administration preliminarily agreed to award up to 6.6 billion US dollars for TSMC's Arizona expansion under the CHIPS and Science Act.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In November 2024 the US Commerce Department finalised the 6.6 billion US dollar CHIPS award, the first major award under the 52.7 billion programme.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: By 2026 TSMC had raised total planned US investment to 265 billion US dollars across up to twelve Arizona fabrication and packaging facilities.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC's first Phoenix fab, Fab 21, is operational, with the rest of the Arizona cluster under construction.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In November 2021 TSMC and Sony formed Japan Advanced Semiconductor Manufacturing to build a fab in Kumamoto; Denso joined the venture in 2022.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: JASM's Kumamoto fab began commercial operations in December 2024 after roughly 8.6 billion US dollars in capital spending.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In August 2023 TSMC committed 3.5 billion euros to a 10 billion-plus euro Dresden fab with Bosch, Infineon and NXP, subsidised with 5 billion euros by Germany.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: The Dresden joint venture, ESMC, plans production across 28-nanometre and 12/16-nanometre capacity.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Taiwan's integrated circuit exports reached 184 billion US dollars in 2022, nearly 25 percent of the island's GDP.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Because leading-edge fabrication is so concentrated in Taiwan, a disruption there could cause another worldwide chip shortage.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In 2017 TSMC invested 3 billion US dollars in Nanjing to build manufacturing capacity in mainland China.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC halted silicon wafer shipments to Huawei and HiSilicon in September 2020 in response to US export controls.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: In October 2024 TSMC reported to the US Commerce Department a potential export-control breach involving one of its most advanced chips.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: To hedge against conflict risk, TSMC expanded into Japan, the United States and Germany from the 2020s onward.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: Japan, the United States and Germany each agreed state subsidies to attract new TSMC fabs.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC said US construction costs ran four to five times an identical plant in Taiwan, making US-made chips at least 50 percent more expensive.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC employs more than 83,000 people and operates fabrication facilities on three continents.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC was the first semiconductor company to join the RE100 initiative, pledging to power all global operations with 100 percent renewable energy by 2050.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: TSMC pledged net-zero emissions by 2050 and recycles more than 85 percent of the water used in fabrication.
beats.label: ARTICLE

beats.text: The important detail is not any single company or machine; it is the dependency between them.
beats.label: THE CONNECTION
